rules.title: Residential rental application screening fees
rules.requirement: A California landlord may charge a residential rental applicant only an application screening fee that does not exceed the landlord’s actual authorized screening costs and the statutory cap, adjusted annually for CPI. The landlord must not charge when no unit is available, must follow one of the statute’s fee/refund screening processes, provide an itemized receipt, return unused amounts, and provide any consumer credit report obtained to the applicant within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: Actual out-of-pocket costs, capped at $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually beginning January 1, 1998

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords or their agents who charge applicants, including guarantors or cosigners, a fee to screen an application to rent or lease residential rental property in California.

rules.exemptions: The section is not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.interaction: The statute states that it does not preempt federal or state housing-assistance rules on deposits and fees, and that nothing prevents a landlord from accepting a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
